# MD-C11 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/full.txt; _text/paged.txt adds PDF page markers and drops blank lines. Page references give the report pagination first and the PDF page in brackets (arabic n = PDF n+4).

Scope: headline claims = Executive Summary (p.4-11, PDF 8-15) and Chapter 6 Conclusions (p.60-61, PDF 64-65). The report has no recommendations section. The Foreword (p.2, by MHCLG) and the chapter summaries (2.10, 3.5, 4.8, 5.5) were not treated as headline locations; where they argue a headline claim with findings, rule 7 was applied. Background, programme description and methods paragraphs of the executive summary were not registered (e.g. "The Pilots established broadly similar referral criteria using a form of the NDT assessment", p.9, a design description). The closing toolkit sentence of the conclusions (p.61) was not registered.

## Rows proposed
- findings: 66 (Q 26, N 40). transformations: 4 (1 crossing strands). claims: 84. relations: 17 (backs 6, covers 11, clashes 0). decisions: header only.
- Joint claims (Q and N roots after tracing transformations): C2 only (fit confirm).
- Empty rests_on: C9, C19, C31, C46, C53, C80.
- Rule 11 merges (executive summary + conclusions): C10, C11, C13, C14, C21, C23, C42, C44, C57, C66, C75-C79. The conclusions sentence on other positive outcomes (p.60) was split across C10, C11, C13, C14, C23 (rule 1).

## Look at first
1. C2 "Qualitative data endorses quantitative findings with clients describing experience of multiple adverse life events" (p.5). The only explicit joint claim. rests_on N baseline findings F1, F3-F5 and Q interview findings F6-F8; the body states the link at p.21 ("Qualitative data echoes these findings") and p.22 ("Both qualitative and quantitative data highlight the prevalence of a range of vulnerabilities"). Proposed fit: confirm. Alternative: by rule 7 the 2.10 sentence also argues C1 with both strands, which would make C1 joint too; A2 kept C1 on the N findings because the executive summary "Results" refers to the baseline questionnaire of 312.
2. C38 (clients and staff gave evidence of positive impacts "across the full range of outcomes quantitively measured") and C82 (improvements in quality of life "even in cases where progress ... may appear negligible in traditional outcomes measures"). Both refer explicitly to the quantitative strand but rest on Q findings only; the text does not cite survey findings at those points. Kept single-strand. If A1 reads the reference to the survey measures as using N findings, C38 becomes joint (confirm) and C82 joint (expand).
3. R10-R12 (C38 backs C16, C11, C21). Basis is the chapter summary 3.5 (p.35): qualitative interviews "provide further evidence" of outcomes "measured through the survey data (e.g. reduced substance use, better health and increased social integration)". The marker is "further evidence" (rule 10). The mapping of "increased social integration" to C11 (people to turn to) and of "reduced substance use" to C21 (reduction in particular drugs, not dependency) is A2's reading.
4. Tension without a clash: Q accounts of "reduced or more stable drug and/or alcohol intake" (F32, p.33; F35 context p.39) against N "no statistically significant reduction" in drug or alcohol dependency (C20, F19). The conclusions reconcile them (C80, C21: "less evidence of significant quantifiable change ... albeit some evidence of a shift toward less harmful patterns"). Both can hold (rule 4); no clashes relation proposed.
5. Tension without a clash: C55 (many clients feel lonely and isolated after moving in, Q) and C10 (loneliness halved at 12 months, N). Different time points and framing; both can hold. No relation proposed.
6. C1-C7, C39: executive summary figures that differ from or are absent in the body. C3: 96% ever rough sleeping (body F1: 91%). C5: depression 80%, anxiety 79%, PTSD, psychosis are not in s.2.5. C6: alcohol dependency figures (49%, 16%, 33%) not in s.2.6. C7: "three-quarters" victims of crime (body: 26% not victims, so 74%). C39 attributes "distance travelled" to clients; the body (p.34) attributes "distance of travel" to stakeholders and delivery staff. rests_on given where the domain matches (rule 8); A1 may judge these partly unsupported.
7. C8 (84% at six months), C9 (housing satisfaction), C14 (65% not victims at six months, "tentative evidence" of a rise at 12 months), C31 (mental health subgroup bullet): these figures come from the separate 12-month outcomes report and are not in the synthesis body. C9 and C31 have empty rests_on; C8 and C14 rest on the 12-month findings for the parts the body reports.
8. C27 vs body: executive summary "relatively consistent pattern of change" vs p.30 "no significant variation"; C29 (younger people improve more on health and alcohol) and C32 (cognitive impairment, alcohol) rest on F26, which reports "some indications" of association and names alcohol and drug dependency together. R13-R17 record C27 covers C28-C32 (the list follows "The most notable differences related to:").
9. C44: denominators differ. Executive summary "512 (of the 1,061)"; conclusions "34% of the total 1,396". 512/1,396 = 36.7%, not 34%; 512/1,061 = 48%. The executive summary also says 884 remained "from a total of 1,061 that had been accepted", while the body (p.36) gives 1,396 accepted and 1,061 housed; Table 5.3 gives 1,387 on the programme at some stage. Registered as one claim with both locations; A1 may split.
10. C77: "More than half" (executive summary, p.11) vs "Roughly half" (conclusions, p.61; s.5.5). Body: £8,429 / £15,880 = 53%. Kept as one row (rule 11).
11. T1 (F59 from F60, crosses yes): the fidelity "scores" (C73) are reported only as "score highly" from the Pilots' internal self-assessments (GMHF, LCRCA, p.46); the evaluation's own fidelity assessments were "a qualitative assessment ... interpreted in line with a scoring guide" (p.16). done_by S1 is approximate: the self-assessment scoring was done by two Pilots, not by the evaluators. Traced to roots C73 is Q only. Alternative: register F59 as Q and drop T1 (no change in the joint count). Same treatment as MD-C8 T1.
12. C79 (good value for money): rests_on F66 (rule 7: p.58 "the comparison of costs and benefits suggests that the Housing First Pilots are providing good value for money") and R8 C78 backs C79 ("This suggests"). The body also reports that with Housing Benefit deducted the BCR is 1.6 and 0.6 and the programme "has so far had a net overall cost to the public finances" (p.58); this qualification is not in the headline claims.

## Other notes
- Rule 3 notes (findings bearing on claims but not linked by the text): fidelity was not linkable to outcomes ("it was not possible to establish whether high fidelity was linked to the achievement of better outcomes", p.46); the CBA states "insufficient evidence to comment authoritatively on the effectiveness of different levels of fidelity" (p.53). WEMWBS results (F63) appear only in the CBA chapter, not in the outcomes chapter.
- Rule 9/13: lived experience groups "provided valuable input into the design of our research tools" (Acknowledgements, p.1). Design-level interface point; not a transformation.
- The CBA chain (T2-T4) stays within the N strand. The Pilots' view that the 30% non-additionality assumption "overestimates non-additional outcomes" (p.56) is a Q statement not used in any estimate.
- C45 compares the 6% death rate with other programmes; the comparison rests on literature (footnote 50), not on a second strand. C46 rests on cited literature only (empty rests_on).
- C53 is a recommendation for practice (rule 6 keeps it); the body (s.4.3) describes relationship building with housing providers but does not argue early engagement; the wording appears in s.4.8 summary only. rests_on left empty.
- C80 has empty rests_on (rule 2) and covers C20 and C24; its "albeit ..." clause was merged into C21.
- No comparison group (p.24, fn 16): the report states outcome changes "cannot formally be attributed to Housing First". Limitation stated by S1, not a finding.
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text; "[...]" marks omissions and " / " separates the wording at different locations in merged claims. Original spellings kept ("quantitively", "dependant", "sustainably", "in in").
